title: 3-Year Treasury Note auction (November refunding new issue) — leg one of three, on Monday because the bond market shuts Wednesday for Veterans Day
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0678 (Quarterly Refunding Statement, released 8:30 AM Wednesday 2026-11-04), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-11-06 (HTTP 200, 75,358 bytes): 'A 3-year note in the amount of $58 billion, maturing November 15, 2029 ... The 3-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Monday, November 9, 2026 ... All these auctions will take place on a yield basis and will settle on Monday, November 16, 2026.' Corroborated same session by the Tentative Auction Schedule PDF (HTTP 200, 27,527 bytes, re-issued with maturity and dated-date columns: 3-Year NOTE, Wed Nov 04 / Mon Nov 09 / Mon Nov 16, maturity Thu Nov 15 2029) and TreasuryDirect securities/announced (CUSIP 91282CRW3, $58,000,000,000, reopening No, issue 2026-11-16). Promoted from estimate on the confirming primary the 2026-09-09 filing named; the 1:00pm ET time is now sourced too. Checked 2026-11-06
notes: CANONICALISED 2026-09-09 from `proposals/treasury-3y-note-2026-11-09.from-treasury-30y-bond-2026-11-12.json` (the only proposal for this id), whose date, new-issue read and Monday-slot reasoning all reproduce against a fresh fetch of the same primary. Two amendments to what the proposal carried. (1) VETERANS-DAY PRECEDENT, narrowed to what this lane's own primary can see: the proposal and the 30Y sibling cite 3-for-3 Monday 3-Year auctions in Veterans-Day-on-Wednesday years (2009, 2015, 2020); `auctions_query`'s 3-Year series starts 2010-02-09, so this lane independently confirms 2015-11-09 and 2020-11-09 (2 of 2 in range) and cannot see 2009 either way. Corroborating, not contradicting. (2) THE MONDAY SLOT IS NOT THE STORY. Monday is ordinary for this security — 44 of 200 auctions since 2010 (22%), 8 of 16 November seats — and in the $58B constant-size era Monday and Tuesday auctions are indistinguishable on demand: bid-to-cover 2.6113 (n=8) vs 2.6123 (n=22), Welch t = -0.02. The same PDF puts the December (12-07) and January (2027-01-11) 3-Years on Mondays too, so the slot is a scheduling pattern rather than a Veterans-Day artifact. EXPECTED SIZE, from the grid rather than any published document: $58B, the 23rd consecutive $58B new issue since 2024-04-09 (`auctions_query`, re-pulled 2026-09-09, zero deviations), behind Treasury's standing 'at least the next several quarters' language. The number becomes published on 2026-11-04, which as a QUARTERLY REFUNDING statement is the document class that actually sets coupon sizes — the size risk on this leg is concentrated on one dated morning rather than spread across the window. CORRIDOR, which is the real difference from the September and October siblings: midterm elections 11-03, refunding statement 11-04, jobs 11-06, THIS AUCTION 11-09, then CPI and the US-China tariff-truce expiry both on 11-10, the bond market shut 11-11, the 30-Year 11-12. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. CONFIRMED 2026-11-06: the 2026-11-04 refunding statement (sb0678) printed the 3-year at $58B, auction Monday 2026-11-09 1:00pm ET, settle 2026-11-16 - the size void clause did not fire; the statement's 'at least' wording was dropped (see the ledger row).
